## Summary

**Root cause:** task-20260726-171957's worker was not actually stalled or looping in its own AI logic — it had already finished all its real work (indexes migration, load-test harness, results doc, 3 commits ahead of main). It was killed by the **kernel OOM killer** mid `next build` inside `quality-gate.sh` (confirmed via `journalctl`: "killed by the OOM killer", 3.7G memory peak, host at 13Gi/15Gi used with swap exhausted from many concurrent `veridian-worker@` Node builds). systemd's `Restart=on-failure` silently restarted the unit, which re-ran the same unbounded-heap build — the resulting checkpoint gap is what the watchdog's staleness check misread as a "stalled"/"periodic checkpoint" signature. `success_count=5` on the known_fixes row confirms several other concurrent RCA tasks hit this identical signature for the same underlying system-wide memory-pressure reason.

**Fix applied:** `/opt/veridian/scripts/quality-gate.sh` (the shared, live-only script every Node-based worker task routes through — not tracked in the repo, same convention as the existing `worker-entrypoint.sh` patches) now exports `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=2048` for Node-project gates, bounding each concurrent build/lint's V8 heap so no single worker can balloon to the memory peak that helped tip the host into OOM. Documented at `ai-os/patches/quality-gate-node-oom-memory-cap-2026-07-26.diff`, committed (e2c9f1c) and pushed.

**known_fixes registered:** `signature="periodic checkpoint", fix_action="restart_unit", success_count=5` — `restart_unit` is already in the watchdog's whitelisted `FIX_ACTIONS`, so step_2 will now actually execute it automatically for this signature.

Checkpointed the RCA task to `pending_review`. Nothing further needed on task-20260726-171957 itself — its own work was already complete.
